doc.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025

title: Choppy and Dumb, 9/11 and humor in his music
summary: The piece evokes dread after 9/11, plays on deliberately dumb sound, and he welcomes laughter.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Speaking of that, parallel notes, “Choppy and Dumb”?
Because I just – I was going to the piano and I said okay, there’s one note here that sustains and then there’s this – I couldn’t figure out the interval.

That’s great. Good listening. I wanted something literally to be like the sort of feeling of kind of like dread. Basically a lot of that’s about looking back a few years at 9/11, New York City. And not that particular track, but some of them were. And oh my God we have kids now, and we’re getting ready to have this beautiful new baby boy, and now 9/11 has just hit New York City so that “Choppy and Dumb” wasn’t literally trying to be that but I wanted these low notes just to be like [scats]. I don't know if I even gave them specific pitches. That’s why you couldn’t figure it out. I just think I told them, “Play any low note and just hold it.” And then – it was a sax quartet. I think I had the sax quartet play – that was written out – [scats]. And they nailed it. They said, “Do you want us to play it like really dumb? Like stupid?” [scats]. “No problem, we can do that.”
It almost struck me like, “All right, play with a junior high tone here.”
Yeah. I actually wanted that. So when they did it they were like, “Are you sure?” And I was like, “Yes, I love that, that’s what I wanted.”
Would you be, if you played that piece in a live situation, would you be offended if people found it to be humorous and started laughing?

No. That would be totally fine. I would not be – I would love it if it made them laugh, I would love that. I don’t have a problem with people – if they laugh just ‘cause they think that’s a stupid sound maybe I wouldn’t like that. But if they laughed because they’re like, “This music has some kind of humor to it and I like that” then great. I’m happy. Yeah. Because a lot of my music does have some humor.
